findings.trigger: The host changes the ID of a live target, then detaches that view or replaces the same-epoch physical target before MutationObserver delivery.
findings.observed: Detach unobserves before consuming the pending live identity difference, retains the old reservation, and records the new physical ID as lastTargetId. After rematerialization the valid current host-later ID conflicts with the stale old reservation, so controls stays absent indefinitely. The same-epoch replacement branch also skips identity classification for the old binding and restores the old ID onto a blank successor. Both generated and explicit identity variants reproduce; delivering the observer before the same transition is a passing control.
findings.expected: Consume the pending live host-ID transition before retiring its current physical binding, invalidate the old reservation, and retain the newly adopted identity through a valid rematerialization/replacement. An ID introduced only after detach remains a distinct rematerialization-conflict case that must fail closed.
findings.impact: Valid relations fail to recover after L1, or a same-epoch successor revives a stale logical identity, depending only on observation scheduling.
findings.fix: Reuse identity provenance reconciliation before unobserving/detaching and before releasing a replaced old physical binding, while preserving the independent-owner and truly-detached authored-conflict rules.
